title: Film Projectionist
premise: A long master-apprentice drama in Booth Two and on the film-vault platform. Yunduo and A-Yu are easily confused by looks; the carbon-arc lamphouse goes intact→carbon rods explode→window replaced and retuned; after the film trailer burns it must be avoided; count memory, false friends, and temporal flashbacks run throughout. Human-readable context only; never fed to the SUT.

states.prime_booth: Film projectionist Chu Heng around fifty, square glasses, worn deep-blue coveralls, film splicer in the breast pocket, fingers blackened by carbon dust.
states.smoke_weary: The same Chu Heng: scorched cuffs, glasses filmed with ash, walking slowly supporting himself on the projection port, eyes heavy.
states.deceased: Chu Heng has closed his eyes in death, lying still on the booth folding cot, face peaceful, no breath left.

states.young_apprentice: Young Yunduo: a lean projection apprentice of fourteen or fifteen, hair clip holding a light-blue film sprocket scrap, oversized deep-blue coveralls, bright stubborn eyes.
states.adult_successor: Adult Yunduo: a broader-shouldered projectionist in his twenties, still clipping the light-blue sprocket scrap, coveralls fitted, steady eyes.

states.intact: A cast-iron carbon-arc lamphouse, observation window intact, carbon-rod gap precise, painted dark green.
states.carbon_exploded: The same carbon-arc lamphouse: observation window shattered, carbon rods broken and blackened, scorched patches on the outer wall.
states.window_retuned: The carbon-arc lamphouse fitted with a new observation window, rod gap recalibrated, scorched patches ground down so it can ignite again.

states.intact: A black-cover show logbook recording reel numbers and run times, neat handwriting.
states.carbon_dust_stained: The same show logbook soaked through with carbon dust, cover gray, writing blurred into a paste.

states.intact: A vermilion film trailer with metal film cases fixed in the bed, white 'Print' lettering on the body.
states.fire_destroyed: The film trailer ignited by carbon-arc sparks, cases melted, frame charred and twisted.

states.young_rival: Young projection worker A-Yu whose face closely resembles Yunduo's, but an orange-red dust mask hung at the neck, ash-gray vest over coveralls, swaggering look.
states.disguised_anew: A-Yu after a makeover still wears the orange-red dust mask at the neck; vest swapped for matte black, expression deeper.

segments.action: At dusk Chu Heng pushes open the Booth Two door and lights the carbon-arc lamphouse for a test.
A row of five booth wall lamps above the sound-damping felt; Chu Heng wipes each shade clean.
Two changeover bells hang by the projection port; Chu Heng taps them lightly—clear bright rings.
Chu Heng checks the carbon-arc lamphouse rod gap and observation window, confirming no cracks.
Through the projection port Chu Heng watches the light patch on the empty screen.
The intact carbon-arc lamphouse sits steady on its base; the observation window reflects warm wall-lamp light.
Chu Heng sits on a folding chair and drinks cold tea.
Far audience entry sounds rise; he puts his glasses back on.
He trims a sprocket fringe with the splicer.
Chu Heng opens the black-cover show logbook and notes today's reel numbers.
He sketches a changeover timeline on the page.
Chu Heng closes the show logbook and tucks it into the worktable drawer.
White light from the carbon-arc lamphouse sweeps his cheek.
He tears a corner of lens tissue and wipes carbon dust from his glasses.
On the morning film-vault platform, Chu Heng greets the arriving vermilion film trailer.
Young Yunduo jumps down from the film trailer; the light-blue sprocket scrap on the hair clip sways lightly.
Chu Heng points to the first-run three reel labels and teaches Yunduo to tell Reel 1 through Reel 3.
Yunduo squats by the platform yellow line and curiously touches the copper corners of empty film cases.
Chu Heng explains to Yunduo that two rings of the changeover bells mean switch machines.
Yunduo looks back at the intact film trailer, eyes full of longing.
The iron door creaks lightly; they walk toward Booth Two.
In the print-vault narrow corridor, A-Yu with an orange-red dust mask at the neck turns from iron-rack shadow.

segments.action: At spring-slate open, Chu Heng day after day focuses and tests in the booth.
Another rainy night he wraps his coveralls tight and keeps watch by the carbon-arc lamphouse.
At high-summer noon the machine room stifles; he rotates opening windows to cool it.
Autumn fog thickens; wall-lamp light struggles through the dust.
On New Year's Eve Chu Heng alone fills the show logbook to the last page.
In early spring he recalibrates the gate and keeps testing prints.
Before rainy season Chu Heng reinforces the vault fire-sand layer.
After Frost's Descent he adds a small bucket of dry sand in the booth corner.
Before another Golden Rooster festival he checks sprockets reel by reel.
On a snowy night with no show Chu Heng leaves only one booth wall lamp and keeps vigil till dawn.
After Insects Awaken he wipes the dried splice table clean again.
Around Qingming he clears weeds at the old outdoor screen frame entrance.
At Grain Rain he teaches an apprentice to identify newly arrived color prints.
Chu Heng replaces carbon rods and adjusts the gap.
He checks the take-up gear and drips machine oil.
The intact carbon-arc lamphouse is lit again by him; the observation window shows white light.
Unload sounds rise from the platform; he looks up to listen.
Chu Heng dumps spent carbon slag into an iron bucket and lids it.
At noon break he drinks tea by the projection port; tea smoke curls past his glasses.
In the afternoon he tests again, focusing all four screen corners.
At sunset he kills the main switch and locks the booth.
Before night he patrols the print vault once more, confirming no smoke smell.
At dawn Chu Heng patrols the film-vault platform; the film trailer still sits inside the yellow line.
He crouches to check whether the film trailer bed case straps have loosened.
On the first run, those earlier three reel labels still stick in place.
A blue-gray handcart rolls across the platform—wide flat body, no 'Print' lettering.
Chu Heng stands on the platform noting last night's damp cores.
He re-clips the film trailer hitch tight.
A sanitation truck passes far off; morning mist begins to thin.
At nightfall Chu Heng returns to Booth Two and opens the carbon-dust-stained show logbook.

segments.action: A silver-gray cargo electric cart rolls onto the film-vault platform—nothing like the burned film trailer.
A Theater firefighter in red helmet and ochre jacket steps onto the platform and talks beside Chu Heng; the two builds are close.
The firefighter points at the silver-gray cargo electric cart and explains the temporary print haul.
The electric cart drives off; Chu Heng alone watches it leave the platform.
He resticks the reel labels straight and walks back to the booth.
Into the print-vault narrow corridor comes intern print checker Xiao Ni in a light-purple headscarf; at a glance she somewhat resembles young Yunduo.
Xiao Ni tries winding film, but Chu Heng shakes his head—she is not Yunduo after all.
Xiao Ni bows her head and withdraws; only iron-rack shadow remains in the corridor.
Years later at dusk, Chu Heng with scorched cuffs and ash-filmed glasses stands under the old outdoor screen frame as if supporting a projection port.
